name: Chain Pause on Failed Loop
description: When any loop in a managed arc (researcher-{plan,gather,synthesize,architect}, reviewer-{research,spec,qa}, builder, dispatch — plus legacy `researcher` / `research-reviewer` for research-iterative configs) fails before emitting its coordinator.next_action triple, no downstream rule fires and the chain dies silently. This rule fires on outcome=failed for those roles and stamps a chain.paused.marker triple so the operator decision surface can render the pause and accept a retry/kill/defer decision. The full ADR-037 §D5 audit triple set is written by the chainpause.Pauser NATS subscriber (cmd/semteams/chainpause/pauser.go) which fires on the same agent.failed.* event. The single rule covers all arcs: adding a new arc means extending the role list, not creating a new rule. ADR-037 §D1 and §D6.

metadata.role_list_rationale: starts_with operator exists (expression/evaluator.go operatorStartsWith) but operates on a single prefix string. Multi-prefix matching via starts_with would need separate conditions with OR logic. Using in with explicit role list is unambiguous and auditable for v1; add new roles when new arcs land. Role name source: agent.loop.role triple predicate (vocabulary/agentic/predicates.go LoopRole). The dispatch researcher role string must be verified against the actual config before deploy.
metadata.triple_split_rationale: The rule engine's add_triple can stamp a simple marker (chain.paused.marker). The full §D5 triple set (chain.paused.cause, chain.paused.classification, chain.paused.error_shape, etc.) requires parsing the LoopFailedEvent.Error field — Go logic, not a template. The chainpause.Pauser NATS subscriber (agent.failed.>) writes those; the rule writes the marker so UI polls see it immediately. Both fire on the same failure event but via different triggers (KV watch vs NATS subject). Using chain.paused.marker keeps the dot-hierarchy uniform: UI and ops-agent queries on chain.paused.* find both the rule's marker and the Pauser's full set.
